main_body: Flat ground patch (dark green mossy tiling texture, 64x48 px), a repeating terrain texture with no standing volume
top_band: none - flat terrain texture; the column shows repeating grass-tuft rows (L 65-105) with no top/front structure
evidence: The kind is terrain (a ground patch), not a standing object, so the top-plus-front contract does not apply. The drawing is a flat, repeating ground texture with tufts and dark speckles and no object volume, no side faces and no elevation view. Nothing here violates the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 8 distinct colours and a median of 8 per tile. The grass reference has 80 colours and a median of 26 per tile, so the candidate is far below it. The paving reference has 7 colours and a median of 7 per tile, but it is a deliberately sparse stone pattern and is not the comparison for this kind. The candidate's tuft and speckle pattern repeats identically every 16 px, which looks mechanical and gives little variation, though the ramp from dark green to light green is visible. It has no flat fills and its dark pixels are tinted green, not neutral black. Against the richer grass reference the candidate is thinner, with a narrow palette and little per-tile variation, so it fails the style bar.
